Update on the Yen.

This one poses more questions than it gives answers.

Ultimately, this one gets into trade management. Remember that the reason we want to see an retracement, is so that we can minimize our risk. We want to place our stop x pips/ticks below the low of the Stop Run (SR) candle. Therefore, the lower price pulls back into the lower shadow, the less our risk will be. Simply put, a pull back into the lower shadow is needed to validate the signal. How much of a pull back into the lower shadow is based on an individual's risk tolerance.

One question that arises is, are we only going to exit with a loss if our stop is hit? If we are only getting out when our stop is hit, we could actually still be long at this moment. Depending on profit targets and position size of course.

Which brings up another issue. As previously stated, we can minimize risk by requiring greater retracements into the lower shadow. Another option is to wait for less of a pull back, but to decrease position size instead.

Now we are starting to get into trade management at this point. So let's come back to this once we have establish what constitutes a valid entry signal............

author: HiddenGap
text:
Here's a couple of examples from the Euro.

Let's start with the long (numbered in black).

Updated rules:

Our count begins with the appearance of a Start Point (SP) candle. The Start Point candle must: (1) have a low lower than the lows of the prior 3 intervals. (2) The long Lower Shadow of the Start Point (SP) candle, must be larger than the combination of its Upper shadow and its body. (3) The Start Point must appear 1-3 intervals after the appearance of a WRB. (4) The long Lower Shadow of the SP candle must be larger than both the lower shadows and the bodies of the 3 intervals Prior to the WRB. This is our #

The Confirmation Candle (CC) must: (1) close lower than the body of the prior candle. (2) have a body larger than the body of the prior candle. In our 5 candle sequence, the CC must be #1, 2,3, or 4

After we have a Confirmation Candle, price must pull back within the Lower Long Shadow of the Start Candle to validate the sequence and trigger entry.

The red count is for a short trade. This count includes the progression of candles.

Notice that the CC candle is #3, not #2. This trade would not have been taken as we are in a SupplyDemand Delta Zone.

Hello my friend. I do not want to spend too much time discussing my current thoughts on volume, but I see things differently from a VSA perspective.

#1a (the WRB): is Climatic Action

#1: is a Shake Out #2: is not a LVT. It is No Demand. This interval makes a higher high and closes higher than the previous interval, so I do not see it at as any kind of a test. So this is No Demand in the wrong place. Which is not uncommon after a couple of Ultra high volume intervals. #3: I would not call this a test. This interval has in increasing range on volume less than the previous two. It is more like No Selling Pressure. This is a sign of strength. #4: since this interval has a lower range than the previous interval and the volume is increasing, this is a squat. Or an example of a low, but increasing, volume test.

text: Here is one from the N.Y. open today. I believe it follows all our rules, please correct me if I'm wrong. The first thing N.Y. did was create a supply zone and then run up back to it to give a hidden up thrust of sorts. While not technically a HU, it was mischievous. SP has a 7 tick upper shadow, bigger than the wicks and or body's of the three candles before our WRB. The confirmation candle looks weak, but it does have a body that closes lower and is larger. The pullback candle gave a good R:R. Now, this may be stretching it on an UT at an important zone but I did see this setting up this morning and hesitated too long while trying to decide what to do. We had weakness in the background for the last three hours and a newly created supply zone right with N.Y. open. This is a backside of the level and in a way a type of continuation trade and they are harder to spot in the heat of the moment (for me).
